subject: Nebula Health — availability & credit framework (SLA negotiation)
messages:
From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@nebulahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: SLA baseline and credit structure questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nebula’s infra and latency profile look promising. Our legal/procurement team reviewed the standard Redwood SLA and we have two asks before we can move to signature:

1) Uptime target: we need 99.99% availability for the hosted inference endpoint used in production.
2) Monthly credits: we prefer a capped credit scheme that limits vendor exposure — specifically, a maximum monthly credit equal to one full month of service fees (rather than per-incident uncapped credits).

We understand there are maintenance windows and the usual exclusions — we’re open to drafting mutually agreeable language that preserves critical maintenance flex. Can you share if Redwood can make an exception on the uptime floor and a cap on credits for enterprise customers (we can take a 12–24 month committed plan)?

Best,
Sam
Sam Rivera
Sr. Manager, Procurement
Nebula Health

[attachment: Nebula_MAL_template.xlsx]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and credit structure questions

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear note and the MAL. Short answer: we can be flexible, but we need to balance operational risk and our standard playbook. I’m outlining a counterproposal below; I’ve looped Rishi for technical context and Laura for commercial/contracting.

Proposed alternative (enterprise commitment):
- Uptime: 99.95% standard for hosted API, with an option to increase to 99.99% for the inference endpoint behind a dedicated capacity reservation (Redwood Dedicated) and a 12-month minimum commit.
- Credits: tiered monthly credit (percentage of monthly invoice) with a hard cap equal to 100% of one monthly invoice. Credit tiers: 99.95–99.9% => 5% credit; 99.9–99.0% => 15% credit; <99.0% => 50% credit. For Dedicated customers we can add a lower band: 99.99–99.95% => 2% credit.
- Maintenance: standard scheduled maintenance excluded with 7-day advance notice. For customers requiring 72 hours notice and blackout windows we can add a contractual commitment when Dedicated is purchased.

I’ll attach a redline (Draft_SLA_Nebula_v2.pdf) that shows the language changes. If Nebula is prepared to commit to a 12-month Dedicated reservation for the production endpoint, we can deliver the 99.99% availability guarantee and the tighter credit math.

Next steps (suggested):
- Please confirm whether Nebula can consider a Dedicated reservation for production (even minimal sizing to start).
- If yes, we’ll produce a redline and a DocuSign-ready contract.

I’m available for a quick call Friday to walk through Rishi’s notes.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.ai]
[attachment: Draft_SLA_Nebula_v2.pdf]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@nebulahealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 14:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and credit structure questions

Sam — quick technical note on Dedicated vs. Hosted:

- Dedicated reservation gives Nebula a pool of GPU capacity with pinned instances and isolated scheduling; that operational isolation is what allows us to commit to 99.99% for the endpoint. For multi-tenant hosted endpoints we rely on elastic routing and best-effort isolation which makes guaranteed 99.99% difficult without a reservation.
- If you adopt Dedicated, we can also offer stricter maintenance windows (we’ll agree to no more than 4 hours/month of scheduled downtime affecting the reserved pool unless there’s a critical security patch).
- Network/edge variability still matters; to reach 99.99% we recommend colocating inference in eu-central-1 region and configuring automatic fallback to a second region (failover cost applies).

Happy to jump on a call to walk through traffic profile requirements — if you can share request rates and P50/P95 latencies we’ll model the sizing.

-Rishi
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@nebulahealth.com>

Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 10:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and credit structure questions

Evelyn, Rishi —

Thanks for the quick responses and the draft. A few follow-ups from legal:

- Nebula is not opposed to Dedicated in principle, but committing to minimum spend is sensitive across our budget cycle. Is there a low-friction pilot sizing that still allows you to provide 99.99% for a single critical inference route? Even a 3-month pilot would help us validate value before the 12-month commit.
- The credit tiers look reasonable, but legal would still prefer a per-incident cap (e.g., maximum credit for a single incident is 50% of the monthly invoice) in addition to the monthly cap you proposed. That prevents one long incident from eroding the entire year of service credits.

Maya and I can share expected QPS and P95; we’ll send numbers by Monday. Also: can you confirm whether SOC2 evidence and uptime historicals for similar customers are available?

Sam

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2026 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: Counterproposal (formal) + evidence package

Sam/Maya — attaching an updated counterproposal and SOC2 summary. Key points in the attached redline (Draft_SLA_Nebula_v2.pdf):

- Pilot option: 3-month Dedicated pilot available at a reduced reserved rate (50% of the committed monthly price) that still qualifies for the 99.99% commitment for the piloted route. If pilot proves successful, we convert to standard Dedicated pricing and a 12-month commitment.
- Incident cap: we can add a per-incident cap of 50% of the monthly invoice in addition to the monthly cap equal to 100% of one monthly invoice.
- Maintenance and notifications: we’ll include a 72-hour scheduled maintenance notification requirement for the reserved pool and allow a one-time annual emergency maintenance exemption (with post-facto report).

We’ve also attached historical availability reports for similarly sized Dedicated customers (redacted) and a SOC2 summary (SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf). The DocuSign link below is a preview of the commercial terms with the proposed SLA redlines embedded — it is not a final signed document.

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign/placeholder-docsign-link/nebula-sla
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/NB-2026-117
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/nebula-sla-2026

If this aligns with Nebula’s legal posture we can route to signature. Laura — can you prepare the 3-month pilot invoice language and a short MSA addendum?

Thanks,
Evelyn
[attachment: Draft_SLA_Nebula_v2.pdf, SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf]

From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@nebulahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Counterproposal (formal) + evidence package

Evelyn — this looks good and the pilot option is exactly what procurement was hoping for. A couple of final asks before we route to legal:

1) Please include explicit language that Nebula will receive 72-hour maintenance notices in writing (email suffices) and define "scheduled maintenance" as an event that will not exceed 4 hours per scheduled occurrence for the reserved pool.
2) We will accept the per-incident 50% cap and the monthly 100% cap, provided there is a maximum of 3 credited incidents per billing period (so credits can’t be multiplied by arbitrary incident counts).

If you accept those two bullets I’ll instruct my legal team to prioritize review and we’ll route to signature. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Sam
Sam Rivera
Sr. Manager, Procurement
Nebula Health
